generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1001, step 1, unique per table; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy an existing parent key value; with probability 0.10 emit NULL (only if column nullable); otherwise pick uniformly from parent keys.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer in [min, max] taken from statistics; include min, min+1, max-1, max.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random string of length 3-12 from a fixed name pool; include near-duplicates (case variants, one-char edits) at 10%.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_code: Random 3-letter uppercase code from a fixed pool; include near-duplicates at 10%.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_enum: Uniform choice from the enum list; include case variants at 5%.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, 5% NULL rows per instance (at least one NULL row per nullable column).

targets.rule: Generate parent rows with no child rows (Student without Has_Allergy) and child rows with NULL FK (Has_Allergy.StuID NULL, Has_Allergy.Allergy NULL).
Include exact literals Cat and Milk, plus case variants cat and milk, in both tables.
Ensure group sizes of 1, 2 and >=3 for GROUP BY StuID and GROUP BY Allergy; include COUNT values 0,1,2,3; include COUNT(col) with NULLs.
Produce groups of size 1, 2 and >=3 for each grouped column.
Create ties at rank 1 for ORDER BY COUNT(*) and ORDER BY column ASC/DESC.
Include rows where Has_Allergy.Allergy IS NULL.
At least 2 rows per group with different Age values.

uncertainty: No calculated columns or date pairs present; formulas limited to range and enum rules. NULL shares estimated at 5% since observed null_rate is 0 but nullable columns exist.
